I’m not sure how I feel about this place. I had high hopes because of the reviews. It wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t great either.

To be fair, this was a Valentine’s Day dinner, so we didn’t get to try the regular menu. However, I do think the restaurant should inform guests when booking reservations that only a Valentine’s Day menu will be served. That wasn’t communicated to us. The portions were generous, and you definitely get a lot of food, but flavor-wise, it was just average. I’ve had much better Italian cuisine.

Starting with the appetizers, the octopus was a strong opener—nicely charred and a very large portion. The baked oysters and clams, however, were a hard pass for me. They were overly oily and heavily breaded, which completely masked the natural flavors of the shellfish.

For the main courses, we ordered scallops with squid ink spaghetti, a ribeye, and a surf and turf. It was a busy night, so perhaps the kitchen was rushed but that shouldn't be an excuse because it was about $80 per person. The spaghetti was just okay, but the scallops were cooked perfectly—tender, not rubbery, and done just right. The ribeye was my mistake; I should have known better than to order steak at an Italian restaurant. I asked for medium rare, but it came out closer to medium. The steak lacked flavor, not juicy and wasn’t particularly impressive, though that’s partly on me for the choice. The surf and turf wasn’t much better. The lobster was overcooked and rubbery, and the steak was well done even though we requested medium. Again, two strikes on the steak potions.

Unfortunately, the highlight of the evening was dessert. It was by far the best part of the meal, and I truly enjoyed it. It’s just disappointing that the rest of the dinner didn’t meet the same standard, especially for the price we paid. Again it isn't the money and it wasn't that bad, it could be a lot better knowing there are many Italian spot to dine out in but a friend wanted to try it.

That said, the service was excellent and the atmosphere was just right. Perhaps it was simply an off night. I would consider giving it another try if I’m in Staten Island again—just not on Valentine’s Day.

Absolutely phenomenal!!

Went here with my wife and my in laws and it was amazing! For starters, the resturant has a great cozy vibe and the staff is so friendly and welcoming!

They give you bread with butter and eggplant caponata which I am a huge fan of!

For appetizers, we got the special fried sweet and sour calamari, minestrone soup, and baked clams. All 3 of which I’d highly recommend! The clams had so much flavor and were in a delicious sauce. The calamari was perfectly crispy and sauced excellently!

For entrees we got the pollo scarpariello, lamb chops, risotto, and veal chop. I personally got the pollo and loved it! The chicken was off the bone which made it so easy to eat and the sauce it was in was perfect! Was light enough so you didn’t feel bogged down but was slammed full of flavor. The rest of my family all loved their meals and we would all happily get what we had again.

For dessert we got a spread of lava cake, cheese cake, carrot cake, panna cotta, and gelato. I thought I was full but I couldn’t stop myself from devouring the lava cake and carrot cake specially. The gelato was also fantastic!

Overall we had such an amazing dining experience! The resturant is family owned and it gives off the family oriented vibe! I cannot wait to go back!

The food and hospitality at Patrizia's of Brooklyn is by far one of the best in all of Staten Island. All of the staff were always friendly and welcoming! Mario consistently took care of my family and I every time that we come here; his friendly, warm, and attentive service is reflective of what exemplary service looks like! Our favorite appetizers are the blackened scallops and octopus carpaccio; the scallops were ALWAYS cooked to perfection where it's both extremely tender and flavorful! The sausage and pepper hero was also extremely delicious, where the sausage is not overly salty but still flavorful and paired perfectly with its tangy and savory sauce! The mushroom truffle pasta is our favorite, including our little toddler who is usually a very picky eater; its creamy but not overly rich, and very savory with perfectly cut mushrooms that's not too thin and provides the perfect bite! What can elevate the dish even more if they gave just a bit more pasta so there's more to enjoy! The pizzas were also perfectly crisp on the exterior and very enjoyable, where the pepperoni was also crisped to perfection! Overall, we have not yet encountered any disappointed dishes just yet, so I highly recommend coming to Patrizia's of Brooklyn for a fun and delicious experience!

Thank you for reading and best of luck! (:

We had a mixed experience at Raval Steakhouse.

The service was the highlight of the evening. The staff was exceptionally friendly, and our waiter was welcoming, attentive, and professional throughout the meal. The atmosphere was also pleasant and romantic. The restaurant was neither loud nor overcrowded, making it suitable for both a date night and a business dinner.

Unfortunately, the food did not meet the same standard, particularly given the prices. We ordered the Dry-Aged Porterhouse ($150) and the Australian Skirt Steak ($62). Both were satisfactory, but neither was particularly memorable considering the cost. We have prepared steaks of comparable quality at home for less than a quarter of the price. Additionally, all of us experienced some stomach discomfort after the meal.

The Watermelon Salad was enjoyable and was likely one of the better dishes we tried. However, the warm bun served at the beginning of the meal was surprisingly bland and lacked flavor.

Overall, I appreciated the excellent service and comfortable, romantic atmosphere, but I did not feel that the quality of the food justified the prices. In my view, the experience was worthwhile for the service and ambiance, but not for the steaks.

Corrado’s Cucina has a nice atmosphere, and after driving by so many times I was excited to finally give it a try. We started with the octopus and the eggplant parmigiana, and both appetizers were enjoyable. The bread  served with ricotta and honey was also excellent and ended up being one of my favorite bites of the meal.

For our entrée, we shared the pappardelle tartufo. The pasta itself was cooked very well, but the dish just wasn’t for me. I knew ordering something outside my usual comfort zone was a bit of a gamble, and unfortunately the flavors didn’t win me over.

We also took home a Nutella pizza for the kids, and that ended up being the biggest hit of the night—it disappeared so quickly I forgot to take a photo before it was gone.

Overall, there were definitely some bright spots, but the experience didn’t quite live up to my expectations. I wouldn’t rule out giving Corrado’s another try in the future, but next time I’d stick with some of the more traditional pasta dishes.

text.text:
Having already visited the Woodbridge location, I was excited to finally experience the original Staten Island restaurant—and it absolutely lived up to the hype.

The atmosphere is intimate, cozy, and effortlessly charming. The cellar setting creates a warm, laid-back vibe that’s perfect for a date night or catching up with friends. There’s even a hidden speakeasy tucked away in the back, which was a fun surprise.

Service was exceptional from start to finish. Our server, June, was warm, attentive, and genuinely made the evening special. She even offered to take photos for us, which was such a thoughtful touch. Manager John also stopped by our table and was incredibly welcoming. If you’ve dined at the Woodbridge location, you may recognize him since he occasionally serves there as well.

Everything we ordered was delicious—the shrimp dumplings, Bang Bang eggplant, burrata, caviar arepas, and chicken satay were all flavorful and beautifully presented.

The star of the evening, however, was the Drops of Jupiter cocktail. This sparkling strawberry-lavender rosé cocktail, complete with shimmering edible glitter dust and garnished with a perfectly ripe strawberry, was every bit as beautiful as it was delicious. Refreshing, lightly floral, and just the right amount of sparkle, it was a truly delectable treat and one of the most memorable cocktails I’ve had in a while.

To top it all off, when we ordered a dessert cocktail after dinner, June happily accommodated our request to split it into two glasses so my friend and I could share it. It’s thoughtful touches like that that elevate an already wonderful dining experience.

Personally, I enjoyed the food here a bit more than I did on my visit to Woodbridge. I think that’s a testament to how well this location has refined its menu over nearly a decade, while Woodbridge is still settling into its stride as a newer restaurant.

Outstanding food, exceptional hospitality, and an inviting atmosphere make this an easy five-star experience. I’ll definitely be back.

📸 I also featured my visit on my foodie pages, @NatEatsNJ on Instagram and TikTok, if you’d like to see the food, cocktails, and atmosphere in action.

text.text:
Not sure if I can say enough great things about the Marina Cafe!

I have been here at least 10 times over the past couple of years and each time I have an excellent experience!

Each meal starts off with hot bread and crackers with butter and olive oil.

For our appetizers we typically rotate between baked clams, fried calamari, meatballs, and the salad. All of the apps are fantastic and my personal favorite is the baked clams!

We have tried a decent amount of the entree at this point as well. Some of the ones we keep going back to are the Pork Chops, Short Rib, Seafood Risotto, Alaskan Salmon, Ahi Tina Steak, Mahi Mahi, and The Rack of Lamb. I am pretty sure my wife has gotten the Lamb more than half of the time we’ve gone here! Most recently I got the Short Ribs and they are delicious!

I am not a huge dessert guy but my family will get the Lava Cake, Affogato, and the Crème Brûlée.

Also want to give a special shoutout to our server Kenny! We’ve had the pleasure of being in his section several times now and he always provides fantastic service!

I would highly recommend Marina Cafe to anyone! We have had many fantastic normal dinners here as well as birthdays, Mother’s Days, and Engagement Celebration!

This was my first visit to the marina several weeks ago and I was very impressed. The floor to ceiling windows offer an incredible view of the marina from everywhere in the restaurant and gives the place a feeling of serenity. Some of the food I tried would rival some of the best Manhattan steakhouse and seafood restaurants. The food was perfectly prepared and plated beautifully
The seafood tower as an appetizer was very impressive with right off the boat fresh tasting clams, oysters, very large shrimp and lobster. The tuna tartare had a very unique and delicious sauce and was mounded on an absolutely delicious fried disk. My other two stand out appetizers were the seafood salad and, a surprise, what they call an Italian eggroll With really delicious Italian red sauce. If you are a lobster bisque lover this lobster bisque was to die for. The Châteaubriand was cooked exactly as ordered, medium rare with house made barbecue sauce and Demi glace which were both excellent with a roasted garlic bulb creamed spinach and mashed potatoes.
The very fresh angry red snapper came on top of broccoli rabe and was topped with very fresh premium crab meat. The best part of this dish for me was the ring of gnocchi around the fish that were like little pillows of softness. The variety of desserts are homemade and all were delicious. If you happen to be there on a nice day and the tiki bar is still open, it is definitely worth sitting out there for a cocktail and a dessert and coffee. I can’t wait to go back there in several weeks for my birthday.

Some of the food I tried would rival some of the best Manhattan steakhouse and seafood restaurants. The food was perfectly prepared and plated beautifully
The seafood tower as an appetizer was very impressive with right off the boat fresh tasting clams, oysters, very large shrimp and lobster. The tuna tartare had a very unique and delicious sauce and was mounded on an absolutely delicious fried disk. My other two stand out appetizers were the seafood salad and, a surprise, what they call an Italian eggroll With really delicious Italian red sauce. If you are a lobster bisque lover this lobster bisque was to die for. The Châteaubriand was cooked exactly as ordered, medium rare with house made barbecue sauce and Demi glace which were both excellent with a roasted garlic bulb creamed spinach and mashed potatoes.
The very fresh angry red snapper came on top of broccoli rabe and was topped with very fresh premium crab meat. The best part of this dish for me was the ring of gnocchi around the fish that were like little pillows of softness. The variety of desserts are homemade and all were delicious. If you happen to be there on a nice day and the tiki bar is still open, it is definitely worth sitting out there for a cocktail and a dessert and coffee. I can’t wait to go back there in several weeks for my birthday.

text.text:
Pastavino offers an energetic atmosphere, excellent service, authentic Italian dishes, and a good selection of drinks and wines. The prices are a bit high for Staten Island and for its distant location and challenging parking (there’s plenty but in a graveled lot, or via valet), yet that is the price for the many good things Pastavino has to offer.

You can quickly detect that the restaurant will move your meal along at a quick, although not too quick pace. I sensed they might do that when I saw a notice from the restaurant about the 90 minute limit for a two person table. I prefer it to be speedy so that’s OK with me. It is worse if it moved too slowly.

Many Staff members will be there to assist your meal along the way, seemingly well trained to pick up a dish, pour you some water, or tend to anything you might need.

The bread is fresh and crispy, and take a look at my photo of the olive oil – – green as olive oil should be. Burn your throat as it should – – perfect!

The pasta – – fresh – – is served hot as pasta should be. Perfect.

The desserts are pricey and though my wife and I got two desserts we probably would shift to one next time since, though good, we probably didn’t need to spend $40 (all in) for them. The gelato is really excellent by the way.

So keep Pastavino in your list of Italian restaurants to go to on Staten Island, even as you stick with your regulars for proximity and value.

The halibut over risotto was smooth and buttery with a lemon caper sauce that hit perfectly. The fried chicken cutlet was crispy, not greasy, and still juicy inside.

The tuna salad was done right, seared clean and paired with fruit and greens that actually worked. Nothing felt random or thrown together.

Service was solid and the place has that warm, slightly upscale but still comfortable feel. Good for a date night or just a nice dinner out.

Not just a place that looks good, the food actually backs it up. Definitely going back.
